chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: Roland Kirk, George Barrow, Jaki Byard and Tommy Turrentine
summary: Short assessments; Kirk used as a tool, Byard rounded out the band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: How about some of the newer players? I thought one of your best bands --
You asked me to call the names, I called the names, man. Stop trying to put the names in. I know who's in my band.
All right.
I don't waste time.
All right.
[long pause]

I may have a few I can call, let me see. I can't really say Roland Kirk. I'd like to say Roland Kirk, but Roland never really fit into my style. He was -- I used him as a tool. I built things around him, when he played in the band.
Barrow, I liked George Barret, the way he played in my band, too. Tenor player, from a long time ago.
He's on that record that you made -- he and Eddie Byrt were on a record. Where was that recorded, at --
At Bohemia.
Yeah, at the Bohemia, yeah. I always liked -- I'll just mention players that I liked who played with you, and I thought the piano player from Boston, Jaki Byard.
Oh, yeah. I forgot about Jackie. I would say Jaki, too. He was well rounded. He rounded the whole band out.
Yeah.
Well, he has such a broad scope of (inaudible) music, anyway. He knew what I was trying to do.
I thought he was good in your bands.
Tommy Turmentine, for a short while, while he was in the band.
Tommy?
Yeah.
I don't think I -- I never did hear him with you. I've heard very little of him, anyway.
At with the Five Spot. He was supposed to with Eric Dolphy, supposed to be in the band when (inaudible) go to Europe with us. He had problems.
